text:
The Islanders are winning on Ilya Sorokin's back, and our numbers are blunt about it. They have a +7 goal difference despite being outchanced by 7.4 expected goals (the quality of chances), and their goaltending has saved 13.1 goals more than expected. Sorokin alone is at 10.9, with a .916 save percentage. Their last win was a 3-2 shootout over St. Louis after trailing in the third, with Bo Horvat scoring in the shootout and Pete DeBoer putting Mathew Barzal back beside Horvat.

Winnipeg's top end is on fire. Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk this month to become the franchise's all-time goal leader, and he has 19 points in his last 10, a run our numbers say he's earned. Kyle Connor had three points in Boston and has 20 goals in 26 games, a start the Jets' own video channel bills as the fastest of the season. We have Connor at 44% to score tonight, the best on either side.

These teams met eight days ago, a 4-3 Winnipeg win in overtime. Logan Stanley faces the Jets for the first time since leaving after 261 games in their colours. Matthew Schaefer, the teenage defenseman setting records on Long Island, is at 76% for a point in our numbers. Kyle Palmieri, Ryan Pulock and Alexander Romanov are out for New York; Dylan DeMelo, Isak Rosen and Vladislav Namestnikov for Winnipeg.

Our numbers have the Islanders at 3.15 expected goals and the Jets at 2.92, close enough that the goalies may decide it. Stuart Skinner starts for Winnipeg, 2.2 goals better than expected this season. In the race they're level: our projection has both finishing around 91 points, the Islanders at 48% to make the playoffs and the Jets at 38%. Dawson Mercer's seven points in ten games is a nice run for Winnipeg, but our numbers read it mostly as bounces, since his chances have been ordinary.
headline: Ilya Sorokin and the Islanders meet the hot Jets
